description:
Residual carve-outs from fz-kdt.97 (2026-08-31, landed as one-contract
rule; widened per the adversarial review's F1), recorded deliberately:

1. CALLABLE-DEMAND returns stand aside from contract_transport_layout: a
   clause set has no lane contract, and the row its demand names is
   fact-derived by exact_direct_callable_layout (fz-9i4.4.5 one-authority;
   forcing the contract broke compiler2_transport_plan_preserves_recursive_
   callable_return_identity, the make(n)->make(n-1) closure-returning
   recursion). A recursion cycle returning a callable can still publish
   disagreeing return forms and lose tail form on those edges. Mixed
   callable|data demands land on the carve-out side identically at every
   view (is_callable = callable-axis-non-empty), so no split-brain.
2. CLOSURE-CARRIED cycles (review F1): the grounded ClosureCallReturn cut
   arm never reports "names an in-component return", so a DATA-returning
   cycle carried ONLY by closure edges keeps evidence forms instead of the
   contract -- the disagreement fz-kdt.97 cures for direct calls persists
   there. Mitigation: the edge is indirect through the boxed apply seam
   (no direct-call tail at stake), behavior byte-identical to base.
   Commented at the arm.

No fixture currently measures a hot callable-returning or closure-carried
recursion, so both costs are unquantified. Fix direction if it ever
matters: a callable-aware contract (the boxed apply seam is the natural
agreed form) for (1); reporting the grounded arm's in-component answer
into the contract trigger for (2), measured against the identity-
preservation test. Sequenced with fz-kdt.96 (all three are callable-side
transport residuals).
title: Callable cycle returns stand outside the one-return-contract rule: disagreeing forms can still demote to Continue
